questions.question: Which is the biggest ocean on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together. It stretches from Asia and Australia to the Americas.

questions.question: Which is the smallest ocean?
questions.explanation: The Arctic Ocean lies around the North Pole. Much of it is covered by sea ice, especially in winter.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in the world?
questions.explanation: Greenland is huge, and ice covers most of it. Australia is bigger, but we call it a continent, not an island.

questions.question: Which ocean lies between Europe and North America?
questions.explanation: Ships and planes cross the Atlantic Ocean every day. Vikings were some of the first Europeans to sail across it.

questions.question: What do we call a piece of land with water on all sides?
questions.explanation: An island can be tiny or huge. Greenland and Zealand are islands, and so is Iceland.

questions.question: What do we call a piece of land with water on three sides?
questions.explanation: A peninsula is joined to a bigger piece of land on one side. Italy is a good example: it sticks out into the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: Which Danish island lies far out in the Baltic Sea, closer to Sweden?
questions.explanation: Bornholm is far from the rest of Denmark. Many people go there by boat, and it is nicknamed the Sunshine Island.

questions.question: Which huge coral reef lies off the coast of Australia?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef is made by tiny animals called corals. It is so big that it can be seen from space.

questions.question: Which canal lets ships sail between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans through Central America?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal cuts through a narrow part of land. Ships save a very long trip around the bottom of South America.

questions.question: Which canal in Egypt lets ships go between the Mediterranean Sea and the Red Sea?
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal saves ships a long trip around Africa. It has no locks, because the two seas are at about the same level.

questions.question: Which warm ocean lies south of Asia, between Africa and Australia?
questions.explanation: The water of the Indian Ocean is warm, and many tropical islands lie in it, such as the Maldives and Mauritius.

questions.question: On which big island in the Indian Ocean do lemurs live?
questions.explanation: Wild lemurs live almost only on Madagascar. Many other animals and plants there are found nowhere else.

questions.question: Which big island lies just off the southern tip of mainland Italy?
questions.explanation: Sicily is part of Italy. A narrow strip of sea, only a few kilometres wide, separates it from the mainland.

questions.question: About how much of the Earth is covered by water?
questions.explanation: Most of it is salty sea water. With so much water, Earth is often called the blue planet.

questions.question: Which country has two main islands, the North Island and the South Island?
questions.explanation: New Zealand lies in the Pacific Ocean, south-east of Australia. Its biggest city, Auckland, is on the North Island.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Denmark and the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The North Sea is fairly shallow and often stormy. Fishing boats and oil rigs work there.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Africa and Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: The Red Sea is warm and has beautiful coral reefs. Its name may come from tiny red algae that sometimes colour the water.

questions.question: What do we call a narrow piece of water that joins two bigger seas?
questions.explanation: A strait can be very busy with ships. The Øresund, between Denmark and Sweden, is a strait.

questions.question: What do we call the land along the edge of the sea?
questions.explanation: Coasts can be sandy, rocky or covered with cliffs. Denmark has a very long coast because it has so many islands.

questions.question: What do we call a group of many islands close together?
questions.explanation: Some countries, such as the Philippines and the Maldives, are archipelagos. Denmark has hundreds of islands too.

questions.question: Which Asian country is made of four big islands and thousands of small ones?
questions.explanation: Japan lies in the Pacific Ocean. Its islands have many volcanoes, and earthquakes happen often.

questions.question: Which part of Denmark is a peninsula, not an island?
questions.explanation: Jutland is joined to the mainland of Europe. The rest of Denmark is made up of islands, such as Funen and Bornholm.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in Denmark itself, not counting Greenland?
questions.explanation: Copenhagen lies mostly on Zealand. The island also has Kronborg Castle at Helsingør, where Shakespeare set his play Hamlet.

questions.question: Which island state belongs to Australia and has a famous "devil" animal?
questions.explanation: The Tasmanian devil is named after the island. Tasmania lies south of mainland Australia, across the sea.

questions.question: What do we call a safe place by the coast where ships can stop?
questions.explanation: A harbour has calm water and shelter from storms. Many big cities, such as Copenhagen, began as harbour towns.

questions.question: Which sea lies east of Denmark and touches Sweden, Germany and Poland?
questions.explanation: The Baltic Sea is less salty than the oceans. It freezes in parts of the north in winter.

questions.question: What is an iceberg?
questions.correct: A big piece of ice floating in the sea
wrong: A cold wind from the north
questions.explanation: Only the top of an iceberg shows above the water. Most of it is hidden below the surface.

questions.question: What do we call a deep, narrow valley in the sea floor?
questions.explanation: Trenches are the deepest parts of the oceans. Light from the Sun never reaches the bottom of them.

questions.question: What do we call a strip of sand or small stones next to the sea?
questions.explanation: Waves carry sand and pebbles onto the beach. The Danish west coast has beaches that go on for many kilometres.

questions.question: Which group of islands in the North Atlantic belongs to the Danish Kingdom and has many sheep and puffins?
questions.explanation: The Faroe Islands have steep green hills and a lot of rain. They lie between Iceland and Norway.

questions.question: Tenerife and Lanzarote belong to which group of islands?
questions.explanation: The Canary Islands belong to Spain but lie off the coast of Africa. They are popular for sunny holidays.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in Europe?
questions.explanation: England, Scotland and Wales are all on the island of Great Britain. Iceland is the next biggest island in Europe.

questions.question: Which of these is usually the biggest body of salt water?
questions.explanation: Seas are smaller than oceans and are often partly surrounded by land. The Baltic Sea is a good example.

questions.question: The islands of Hawaii lie in which ocean?
questions.explanation: Hawaii is made of volcanic islands far out in the Pacific Ocean. It is thousands of kilometres from any continent.

questions.question: What do we call a pointed piece of land that sticks out into the sea?
questions.explanation: A cape often has a lighthouse to warn ships. The North Cape in Norway is a famous one.

questions.question: Which island is nicknamed the Emerald Isle because of its green fields?
questions.explanation: Ireland gets a lot of rain, so the grass stays bright green. The island lies west of Great Britain.

questions.question: Which Italian city is built on more than a hundred small islands?
questions.explanation: Venice has canals instead of roads for cars. People travel by boat, and many buildings stand on wooden poles in the water.

questions.question: Orkney and Shetland are islands near the north coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Orkney and Shetland are known for strong winds, seabirds and ancient stone houses. Vikings once ruled there.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Turkey in the south and Ukraine in the north?
questions.explanation: The Black Sea's deep water has very little oxygen, so old shipwrecks on its floor are very well preserved.

questions.question: Which strait splits the city of Istanbul between Europe and Asia?
questions.explanation: Bridges and tunnels join the two sides of Istanbul. Ships sailing in or out of the Black Sea must pass through the Bosphorus.

questions.question: Which strait links the Atlantic Ocean to the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Spain and Morocco face each other across the Strait of Gibraltar. At the narrowest point it is only about 14 kilometres wide.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in the Caribbean?
questions.explanation: Cuba is a long, narrow island at the northern edge of the Caribbean Sea. Hispaniola is the second biggest.

questions.question: Borneo is shared by Indonesia, Malaysia and which other country?
questions.explanation: Borneo is a huge island with old rainforests. They are home to orangutans, which live in the wild only on Borneo and Sumatra.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Sicily is part of Italy, and its biggest city is Palermo. The island lies near the centre of the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: The Galápagos Islands, linked to Charles Darwin, belong to which country?
questions.explanation: The islands lie in the Pacific Ocean, about 1,000 kilometres from the coast. Darwin visited them in 1835 and studied the animals.

questions.question: Easter Island, famous for its giant stone statues, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Easter Island is one of the most remote inhabited islands. It lies in the Pacific Ocean, more than 3,000 km from Chile.

questions.question: Madeira and the Azores are islands in the Atlantic that belong to which country?
questions.explanation: Both island groups are volcanic. Madeira is known for its flowers and the Azores for hot springs and green hills.

questions.question: Which is the biggest Greek island?
questions.explanation: Crete was home to the Minoans, who built great palaces, such as Knossos, more than 3,500 years ago.

questions.question: Which island is the second biggest in the Mediterranean Sea?
questions.explanation: Sardinia is part of Italy and lies west of the mainland. It has many ancient stone towers called nuraghi.

questions.question: Corsica, the birthplace of Napoleon, belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Corsica is a mountain island close to Italy but part of France. Napoleon was born there in 1769.

questions.question: Which island country lies just off the southern tip of India?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka is shaped a little like a teardrop. It is famous for its tea and its elephants.

questions.question: Which ocean trench contains the deepest known place on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific is deeper than Mount Everest is high. Its bottom is almost 11 kilometres below the surface.

questions.question: Which warm flow of ocean water helps keep north-west Europe mild?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream starts near Florida, and its warm water flows on across the Atlantic. Without it, Europe's winters would be colder.

questions.question: Which cape in South Africa was a key point on the sea route from Europe to India?
questions.explanation: Ships sailed around the Cape of Good Hope before the Suez Canal opened. Vasco da Gama passed it in 1497.

questions.question: The Kiel Canal in Germany links the North Sea with which other sea?
questions.explanation: Ships use the Kiel Canal to avoid the long trip around Denmark. It saves a lot of time and fuel.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Greece and Turkey?
questions.explanation: The Aegean Sea is full of islands, such as Lesbos, Rhodes and the Cyclades. Ancient Greek sailors knew it very well.

questions.question: Which sea lies between Australia and New Zealand?
questions.explanation: The Tasman Sea is named after the Dutch explorer Abel Tasman. He sailed there in 1642.

questions.question: Which sea lies off the west coast of India?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea is part of the Indian Ocean. Seasonal winds called monsoons have helped traders cross it for thousands of years.

questions.question: Which large bay lies east of India and west of Myanmar?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Bengal is one of the biggest bays in the world. Great rivers, such as the Ganges, flow into it.

questions.question: Which island in the eastern Mediterranean lies south of Turkey?
questions.explanation: Cyprus is the third biggest island in the Mediterranean. Copper was mined there long ago, and the word copper comes from its name.

questions.question: Zanzibar, an island with spice farms, lies off the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: Zanzibar lies in the Indian Ocean. For centuries it was a busy trading place for spices such as cloves.

questions.question: Papua New Guinea shares its main island with which other country?
questions.explanation: New Guinea is the second biggest island in the world. Papua New Guinea has its eastern half and Indonesia its western half.

questions.question: Which group of islands lies off the west coast of Scotland?
questions.explanation: The Hebrides include Skye, Lewis and Islay. Many people there speak Scottish Gaelic.

questions.question: Which Arctic island group belongs to Norway and is known for polar bears?
questions.explanation: Svalbard lies far north of the Arctic Circle. A global seed vault there keeps seeds safe for the future.

questions.question: What was the "Northwest Passage" that explorers searched for?
questions.correct: A sea route north of Canada
wrong: A sea route north of Russia
A pass through the Rocky Mountains
questions.explanation: Explorers wanted a short sea route from the Atlantic to the Pacific. Ice made it very hard, and Roald Amundsen first sailed it from 1903 to 1906.

questions.question: Spain and Portugal share which large peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Iberian Peninsula is in south-west Europe. The Pyrenees mountains separate it from France.

questions.question: Norway and Sweden share which large peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Scandinavian Peninsula is the biggest in Europe. Denmark is not on it, but it is close by.

questions.question: Yemen and Oman lie on which large peninsula?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Peninsula is mostly desert, and Saudi Arabia covers most of it. It is one of the biggest peninsulas in the world.

questions.question: What is a fjord?
questions.correct: A long sea inlet between steep cliffs
wrong: A ring of coral around an island
A big lake inside a volcano
questions.explanation: Glaciers carved fjords long ago, and the sea filled the valleys. Norway is famous for its fjords.

questions.question: Which sea has the Isle of Man in the middle of it?
questions.explanation: The Irish Sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland. Ferries cross it from Wales, England and Scotland.

questions.question: Which ocean is named after a country?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is named after India, which sticks out into it. Traders sailed it for thousands of years.

questions.question: Which Greek island was shaped by a huge volcano and is famous for white houses above a sea-filled crater?
questions.explanation: A giant eruption more than 3,500 years ago blew out the middle of the island. What is left is a ring of cliffs around a bay.

questions.question: Mount Fuji and Tokyo are both on which Japanese island?
questions.explanation: Honshu is the biggest island of Japan. It has most of Japan's big cities.

questions.question: The Suez Canal is the border between which two continents?
questions.explanation: That makes Egypt a country in two continents. Most of it is in Africa, but the part east of the canal is in Asia.

questions.question: What is an atoll?
questions.explanation: An atoll is a ring of coral around a lagoon. The Maldives are made up of many atolls.

questions.question: Which strait separates Russia from Alaska?
questions.explanation: The Bering Strait is less than 90 kilometres wide at its narrowest. It is named after Vitus Bering, a Danish explorer who sailed for Russia.

questions.question: Newfoundland, an island in the Atlantic, is part of which country?
questions.explanation: Vikings landed in Newfoundland about a thousand years ago. Fishing was the island's main work for centuries.

questions.question: Which bay lies off the north coast of Spain and the west coast of France?
questions.explanation: The Bay of Biscay is part of the Atlantic Ocean. Its waters can be rough and stormy.

questions.question: Which peninsula in north-west France juts out into the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: Brittany has a rocky coast and a Celtic culture. Its name is related to the name of Britain.

questions.question: Which sea separates Italy from the Balkan Peninsula, with Venice at its northern end?
questions.explanation: The Adriatic Sea is long and narrow. It is part of the Mediterranean, and Croatia has a coast full of islands along it.

questions.question: Tahiti, an island in the South Pacific, belongs to which European country?
questions.explanation: Tahiti is the biggest island of French Polynesia, and the town of Papeete on Tahiti is its capital.

questions.question: At the northern tip of Denmark near Skagen, the Skagerrak meets which other body of water?
questions.explanation: At Grenen, near Skagen, waves from two seas crash together. The Skagerrak and the Kattegat flow into each other.

questions.question: Which strait separates the Danish island of Funen from Jutland?
questions.explanation: The Little Belt is narrow, and two bridges cross it. The Great Belt is a different strait, between Funen and Zealand.

questions.question: Which two big Danish islands lie south of Zealand?
questions.explanation: Lolland and Falster are low and flat, with fertile farmland. Bridges and a tunnel link them to each other.

questions.question: Iceland sits on which long underwater mountain chain?
questions.explanation: The ridge is where two plates of the Earth's crust move apart. Iceland is one of the few places where it rises above the sea.

questions.question: Which island off Iceland was formed by an undersea volcano in 1963?
questions.explanation: Surtsey appeared out of the sea during several years of eruptions. Scientists have watched how plants and animals arrived there.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in Sweden?
questions.explanation: Gotland lies in the Baltic Sea. Its main town, Visby, has a well-kept medieval wall.

questions.question: The Åland Islands, where most people speak Swedish, belong to which country?
questions.explanation: The islands lie between Sweden and Finland. They govern themselves and, under old treaties, have no armed forces.

questions.question: Which gulf in the northern Baltic Sea lies between Sweden and Finland?
questions.explanation: Much of the Gulf of Bothnia freezes in winter. Ships there often need icebreakers.

questions.question: Which sea in the Atlantic Ocean has no coast and is named after a floating seaweed?
questions.explanation: The Sargasso Sea is bounded by ocean currents instead of land. European eels swim there to lay their eggs.

questions.question: The name of which ocean comes from a Greek word for "bear"?
questions.explanation: The Greek word arktos means bear. The Greeks named the far north after the Great Bear, a group of stars in the northern sky.

questions.question: Which famous cape lies at the southern tip of South America?
questions.explanation: Cape Horn is known for rough seas and strong winds. Sailors feared the trip around it.

questions.question: Which strait near the southern tip of South America is named after an explorer who sailed for Spain?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand Magellan found this route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans in 1520. It is a winding passage with strong winds.

questions.question: In which year did the Suez Canal open?
questions.explanation: It opened after about ten years of work. The Panama Canal followed in 1914.

questions.question: Which strait is the narrowest part of the English Channel?
questions.explanation: On a clear day you can see France from the white cliffs of Dover. The Channel Tunnel runs under this strait.

questions.question: Which strait separates Sicily from mainland Italy?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Messina is only about three kilometres wide at its narrowest. Old Greek stories placed the monsters Scylla and Charybdis there.

questions.question: The Dardanelles links the Aegean Sea with which small sea?
questions.explanation: Ships from the Aegean pass through the Dardanelles and cross the Sea of Marmara. Then the Bosphorus leads on to the Black Sea.

questions.question: Which strait lies between Malaysia and the Indonesian island of Sumatra?
questions.explanation: Ships sailing between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific often use the Strait of Malacca. It is a very important sea route.

questions.question: Which strait separates Tasmania from mainland Australia?
questions.explanation: It is named after George Bass, a British explorer. Strong winds and big waves can make it hard to cross by boat.

questions.question: Which stretch of sea separates Madagascar from the African mainland?
questions.explanation: The Mozambique Channel lies in the Indian Ocean. Long ago, Madagascar broke away from Africa and drifted off.

questions.question: Which island at the southern tip of South America is shared by Chile and Argentina?
questions.explanation: The name means "Land of Fire" in Spanish. Early sailors saw fires lit by the people who lived there.

questions.question: Which is the biggest island in Germany?
questions.explanation: Rügen lies in the Baltic Sea and is famous for its white chalk cliffs. A bridge and a causeway link it to the mainland.

questions.question: The narrow Corinth Canal cuts through land in which country?
questions.explanation: The Corinth Canal is only about 6 kilometres long. It cuts across a strip of land, so ships do not need to sail around a peninsula.

questions.question: Singapore is an island country at the southern tip of which peninsula?
questions.explanation: A causeway and a bridge link Singapore to Malaysia. Singapore also has many smaller islands around its coast.

questions.question: Which volcanic peninsula in the Russian Far East is known for bears and hot springs?
questions.explanation: Kamchatka has more than a hundred volcanoes. It is so remote that most visitors arrive by plane.

questions.question: Which desert peninsula lies between the Gulf of Suez and the Gulf of Aqaba?
questions.explanation: Sinai is the part of Egypt that lies in Asia, east of the Suez Canal. Its south is rocky and mountainous.

questions.question: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which Australian state?
questions.explanation: The reef is about 2,300 kilometres long. It lies in the Coral Sea, off Australia's north-east coast.

questions.question: Which sea north of Norway and Russia is named after a Dutch explorer?
questions.explanation: Willem Barentsz explored the Arctic in the 1590s. Warm Atlantic water keeps the southern part of the sea free of ice all year.

questions.question: After his defeat at Waterloo, Napoleon was sent to which remote island in the South Atlantic?
questions.explanation: Saint Helena is thousands of kilometres from Europe, so he could not escape. He died there in 1821.

questions.question: The name "Mediterranean" comes from Latin words meaning what?
questions.correct: In the middle of the land
questions.explanation: The Romans saw the sea as lying in the middle of the lands they knew. Europe, Africa and Asia all touch it.

questions.question: Which strait links the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden?
questions.explanation: The name means "Gate of Tears" in Arabic. It lies between Yemen and the Horn of Africa.

questions.question: Which cape is the southernmost point of Africa?
questions.explanation: Cape Agulhas in South Africa marks where the Atlantic and Indian Oceans are said to meet. Many people think the Cape of Good Hope is further south.

questions.question: What do we call a narrow strip of land that joins two bigger pieces of land, like Panama?
questions.explanation: The Isthmus of Panama joins North and South America. The Panama Canal cuts right across it.

questions.question: Which Baltic island is shared by Germany and Poland?
questions.explanation: Usedom is known for sandy beaches and old seaside towns. The border between Germany and Poland runs across it.

questions.question: Which strait separates the North Island and the South Island of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Cook Strait is named after Captain James Cook. Ferries cross it, though the sea can be rough.

questions.question: Which peninsula in south-east Mexico separates the Gulf of Mexico from the Caribbean Sea?
questions.explanation: The Yucatán Peninsula was home to the Maya. Their stone cities, such as Chichén Itzá, can still be visited.
